item.title: From GPT to agents: how AI changed on Hacker News
item.description:
This week I revived my Hacker News dataset. It is every story and comment from 2007 until this week, about 50 million rows, as monthly Parquet files that DuckDB can query directly. Having it fresh again, I wanted to ask one simple question.

How did the conversation about AI actually change?

Not “is AI big”, that one is obvious. I mean what people talk about, who they talk about, and how they feel about it. Hacker News is a decent microscope for this. It is a developer crowd, it is very online, and it reacts to everything within hours.

item.title: Using Nano Banana Pro as 'Browser Engine'
item.description:
Randomly I am thinking can we use the Google new Nano Banana Pro model as a “browser engine”? The goal was to see how it handles rendering a standard HTML page compared to a modern web browser.

The Setup

I asked ChatGPT 5.1 Thinking to create it with this prompt

Create a html for a mock business profile landing page 
about independently owned convenience store. It should
be 1 file contain all the html js css

It happily produce 1700 line length HTML page for it. You can view the full page here.

item.title: Smolagents
item.description:
The next iteration of agents?

LLM + function calling + ReACT is the usual way. But it can only call predefined functions with predefined arguments.

But smollagents do the function calling as part of code exection. It have Python runtime as part of the agent chain of thoughts.

So it can call and compose the functions, do iteration, and pass larger amount of data between call (pass the whole pandas dataframe, for example).
